facts.text: Cole joined Denver in 1874, stretching north from Martin Luther King Blvd. into the city’s historic core.
The Wyatt School, a clean‑brick landmark built in 1887, still stands at 3620 Franklin St. as a testament to Cole’s early education history.
Cole’s name honors Carlos M., a pioneer who helped shape the neighborhood’s identity in the late 19th century.
Cole was an early Denver Public Schools superintendent who pioneered the city’s junior high model, influencing education nationwide.
The 1888 Swedish Evangelical Lutheran Church was later repurposed into housing, reflecting Cole’s adaptive reuse of historic buildings.
Over the past decade, Cole has seen revitalization and gentrification, with new residential projects emerging beside preserved historic homes.
